Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and agreed on a short pilot and doc handoff.
topics: SSO / SAML integration and RBAC mapping
Audit logs, retention windows, and export capabilities
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-07
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Petrichor Head of IT), Samir Patel (Security Engineer), Evelyn Cho (CTO)

Summary: quick intake to surface security gating criteria and decide whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense for their student-data workloads (FERPA).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick run through who we have?
[00:12] Marta: hi i'm Marta, head of IT at Petrichor, thanks.
[00:15] Samir: samir here, security eng - i look after infra and compliance checks.
[00:18] Evelyn: evelyn, cto, i'll be listening for deployment constraints and cost signals.
[00:22] Priya: priya from the solutions eng team, i'll handle the technical details on keys, audit logs, network.

[00:45] Jordan: goal for today - map your gating criteria: SOC-2/ISO or any certs, sso and rbacs, encryption, retention, and whether you need private deployment. then we can propose a pilot. sound right?
[00:58] Marta: yeah that's it. primary is FERPA and student pii - we need to know how long logs live, who can see them, and where the data sits.

[01:15] Priya: quick headliner: Redwood supports hosted api, dedicated capacity, and private vpc/on-prem. for security evidence we have SOC2 type II reports, and an iso 27001 overview — we'll share the attestation.
[01:33] Samir: when you say "share" — do you provide full reports or redacted summaries? our vendor policy usually requires the full third-party attestation or a bridge letter.
[01:44] Priya: we can provide the SOC2 report via an executed NDA and a secure link; for ISO we have a summary plus the cert — typical process. we'll send specifics.

[02:02] Marta: on sso, we run OKTA. we need SAML 2.0 integration and want user provisioning so non-admins can't create API keys. we also want SCIM provisioning into RBAC groups.
[02:20] Priya: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user/group sync. RBAC can be mapped to your groups - role mapping is flexible. small caveat: if you go private on-prem, you own the idp connectivity; for hosted we integrate via SAML with SP initiated flow.

[02:48] Samir: audit logs — can we get a copy of logs in near-real time? we require immutable audit trails and 1 year retention as baseline, sometimes 3 years for selected events.
[03:05] Priya: logs are captured per-token and per-request; we retain logs in the control plane with configurable retention windows. for dedicated/private we can offer longer retention and log export to your S3/Cloud Storage or SIEM.
[03:23] Jordan: important note: hosted tier's default retention is 90 days, but we can customize for enterprise customers with a contract addendum.

[03:40] Marta: encryption — we need customer-managed keys (BYOK) for at-rest encryption. is that supported?
[03:48] Priya: yes, both dedicated and private support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration. hosted can be configured with a customer-managed KMS in many regions — there are some network and ops requirements (we'll list them).
[04:05] Samir: do we get key rotation logs and access audit for the KMS? we need proof of who used keys and when.
[04:12] Priya: you can configure key usage auditability; if you're using your own KMS (e.g., AWS KMS), you get CloudTrail logs. we also emit events into the audit log that tie back to key operations, but exact artifact depends on deployment mode.

[04:35] Evelyn: can you walk the tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private for our use case — low-latency campus apps vs batch scoring overnight?
[04:47] Jordan: hosted is fastest to onboard, best unit cost for bursts; dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and isolation with stronger SLAs; private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full data control and residency but more ops overhead.
[05:05] Priya: for FERPA areas we usually recommend dedicated with customer-managed KMS or private if you need physical isolation and strict data residency.

[05:25] Samir: network segmentation — we need to ensure traffic never traverses public internet for student pii. what are options?
[05:32] Priya: private peering (VPC peering or Direct Connect), or a private deployment in your network. for hosted we can set up VPC peering to avoid public internet; dedicated usually sits in a private subnet. we'll provide a network diagram.

[06:00] Marta: data residency — we need all data for CA students to stay in US-West. does Redwood provide region pinning?
[06:08] Priya: yes, you can pin models and traffic to specific regions; with dedicated or private we can guarantee processing region. hosted has region options but we need to verify exact SLA for geo-locking in contract.

[06:30] Jordan: compliance checks — any regulatory flavors? you mentioned FERPA, anything else like state-level data laws?
[06:38] Marta: primarily FERPA, plus a couple state privacy laws. we need support for data deletion requests too.

[06:50] Samir: deletion — can we purge conversation data on demand and get confirmation?
[06:56] Priya: yes, we support data deletion workflows. for hosted we can delete records and you can request audit evidence. with private/dedicated you have faster control and can remove local caches/keys. note: model KV caches are ephemeral but we'll document retention.

[07:20] Samir: about model fine-tuning or logs used for training — we have a strict ban on using customer data for model training. how is that enforced?
[07:28] Priya: by default we don't use customer data to train public models. we have contracts and settings that opt-out of telemetry; for enterprise we can disable telemetry and training pipelines entirely and produce an attestation.

[07:48] Jordan: question about audit logs format — do you export to Splunk/Datadog?
[07:53] Priya: yes, we provide syslog/forwarders and S3 export; integrations include Splunk, Datadog, ELK — we'll share the export schema.

[08:10] Marta: can we get a live demo of the RBAC mapping and SAML flow? that would help our identity team.
[08:17] Jordan: yes — we can schedule an identity-focused demo with our SEs; priya can lead it and show SCIM mapping, role sync and provisioning flows.

[08:35] Samir: network egress — do you support static egress IPs for firewall allowlisting?
[08:40] Priya: for dedicated/private we can provide stable egress ranges; hosted is more dynamic but we can provide ranges per region or set up private peering to avoid egress issues.

[08:58] Evelyn: incident response — do you provide post-incident reports and forensics access?
[09:04] Priya: yes, enterprise plans include incident response support, and we share forensic logs. response SLAs are part of dedicated/enterprise contracts.

[09:20] Samir: about encryption in transit — TLS is standard, but we need mutual TLS for some internal services. supported?
[09:27] Priya: mutual TLS is supported for private deployments; for hosted/dedicated we support mTLS for certain endpoints and support VPN/Direct Connect options. we'll map out which endpoints.

[09:50] Jordan: quick clarifier — does Petrichor anticipate PII hitting the prompt layer or only hashed ids?
[09:56] Marta: both. teachers will upload student essays (PII), and apps will send identifiers. so we need end-to-end controls.

[10:10] Priya: that pushes us to dedicated/private recommendations. also we suggest tokenization and prefix caching controls so raw PII isn't stored in logs unless necessary.

[10:30] Samir: do you have a data processing agreement and a subprocessor list?
[10:35] Jordan: yes, we have a DPA and a current subprocessor list — will share redacted vendor names as needed.

[10:50] Marta: retention again — for auditability we might want a 3-year window for authentication events and 1 year for request payloads. possible?
[10:58] Priya: yes for dedicated/private we can meet that; hosted we can extend retention with storage add-ons. we'll add retention SLAs into the pilot proposal.

[11:20] Evelyn: curious about performance — if we go dedicated with quantized models, what's the latency tradeoff?
[11:27] Priya: quantization reduces cost and memory, small latency improvement; dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels yield predictable latency. we'll propose perf profiles for campus daytime loads vs nightly batch.

[11:45] Samir: penetration testing — can we run our own pen test against the deployment?
[11:51] Priya: yes, for dedicated/private we allow customer pen tests with coordination; hosted pen tests require a scope and a date and we may run co-ordinated whitebox tests.

[12:10] Jordan: any blockers from your side for moving to a pilot?
[12:15] Marta: we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration details, and to confirm FERPA deletion flow.
[12:22] Samir: plus exact retention windows and proof of SSO/SCIM provisioning.

[12:35] Priya: action plan: i'll send SOC2/ISO docs and a network diagram; jordan will send pricing; samir will share retention policy; then we schedule pilot scoping.

[12:55] Jordan: noted. quick question on cost sensitivity — is price a hard blocker or negotiable?
[13:02] Evelyn: price matters but security and compliance are higher priority; if dedicated solves our gating, we can budget.

[13:20] Samir: one more on audit logs — can logs be tamper-evident? we prefer immutable storage.
[13:26] Priya: yes, we can stream to write-once storage or your SIEM with object lock policies. we'll include that as an option.

[13:40] Marta: okay. timeline — we want a pilot in Q3, ideally start mid-august.
[13:46] Jordan: we can aim for a pilot kickoff 2027-08-17 week, pending docs.

[14:00] Priya: i'll attach sample config for SAML, SCIM, and the RBAC JSON mapping and a sample network diagram.

[14:12] Samir: for KMS — if we bring our own keys via AWS KMS, what's the integration surface? will the key ever leave our control?
[14:20] Priya: your key policies are enforced by your KMS. Redwood requests cryptographic operations, but keys remain in your KMS/HSM; we don't extract raw key material. we'll provide the exact call flow.

[14:40] Jordan: small note — some of our customers call the product names slightly different, you may see 'Redwood Dedicated' or 'Redwood Private' mis-typed in docs but same underlying options.

[15:00] Marta: any other compliance certs you plan to support? we may need SOC2 plus an ISO checklist.
[15:07] Priya: we maintain SOC2 type II; ISO 27001 is in our compliance pack. for education-specific controls (FERPA) we'll map how our features meet controls and produce a gap table.

[15:28] Evelyn: ok that's helpful. next steps we discussed — timeline and doc handoffs.

[15:40] Jordan: great — we'll follow up with the documents and schedule the identity demo and the pilot scoping. thanks all.

[15:48] Marta: thanks everyone.
[15:50] Samir: thanks.

End of transcript.
